edition.description: Nine chapters, as in the 1925 first edition.

characters.name: Nick Carraway
characters.summary: The narrator: a Yale man from the Midwest who rents a small house in West Egg in 1922 to learn the bond business.

characters.name: Jay Gatsby
characters.summary: Nick’s mysterious, fabulously rich neighbour, famous for his lavish parties.

notes.text: Jordan reveals he loved Daisy in 1917, before he went to war.
Was born James Gatz in North Dakota and reinvented himself under the copper millionaire Dan Cody.
Tom exposes his fortune as bootlegging. He resolves to take the blame for the car that killed Myrtle.
Is shot dead in his pool by George Wilson.

characters.name: Daisy Buchanan
characters.summary: Nick’s charming second cousin once removed, living in East Egg with her husband Tom.

notes.text: Married Tom in 1919 after Gatsby went overseas.
Was driving Gatsby’s car when it struck and killed Myrtle Wilson.
Has left with Tom, sending no word to the funeral.

characters.name: Tom Buchanan
characters.summary: Daisy’s enormously wealthy, arrogant husband, once a Yale football star.

notes.text: Admits to Nick that he told Wilson whose car it was.

characters.name: Jordan Baker
characters.summary: Daisy’s friend from Louisville, a cool, sardonic professional golfer.

notes.text: Nick recalls a rumour that she cheated in her first big tournament.

characters.name: Myrtle Wilson
characters.summary: Vital, discontented wife of a garage owner in the valley of ashes.

notes.text: Is struck and killed by Gatsby’s car.

characters.name: George Wilson
characters.summary: Myrtle’s spiritless husband, who runs a garage in the valley of ashes.

notes.text: Discovers Myrtle has a lover and plans to take her West.

characters.name: Catherine
characters.summary: Myrtle’s sister, who repeats rumours about Gatsby.

characters.name: Michaelis
characters.summary: Young Greek who runs the coffee shop next to Wilson’s garage.

characters.name: Owl Eyes
characters.summary: Bespectacled party guest astonished that the books in Gatsby’s library are real.

notes.text: Is one of the very few at Gatsby’s burial.

characters.name: Meyer Wolfsheim
characters.summary: Gatsby’s associate, a gambler said to have fixed the 1919 World Series.

notes.text: Refuses to come to Gatsby’s funeral.

characters.name: Klipspringer
characters.summary: Freeloading guest who lives at Gatsby’s house — “the boarder”.

notes.text: Telephones after Gatsby’s death only to ask for his tennis shoes.

characters.name: Dan Cody
characters.summary: Copper millionaire on whose yacht the seventeen-year-old James Gatz found his new life.

characters.name: Henry C. Gatz
characters.summary: Gatsby’s father, who comes from Minnesota for the funeral.

phases.label: Cousins
phases.note: She is his second cousin once removed.

phases.label: Married
phases.note: Tom’s affair with “some woman in New York” is an open secret.

phases.label: Married
phases.note: At the Plaza, Daisy cannot say she never loved Tom, and returns to him.

phases.label: College acquaintances
phases.note: They knew each other at Yale.

phases.label: Old friends
phases.note: They grew up together in Louisville.

phases.label: Broken off
phases.note: Nick ends it before leaving the East.

phases.label: Affair
phases.note: He keeps an apartment in the city for them; breaks her nose when she says Daisy’s name.

phases.label: Married
phases.note: She despises him.

phases.label: Married
phases.note: He discovers her infidelity and locks her up.

phases.label: Strung-along customer
phases.note: Tom dangles the sale of a car to Wilson.

phases.label: Fatal tip
phases.note: Tom told Wilson the yellow car belonged to Gatsby.

phases.label: Neighbours
phases.note: Gatsby introduces himself at a party.

phases.label: Go-between
phases.note: Nick hosts Gatsby’s reunion with Daisy.

phases.label: Loyal friend
phases.note: Nick tells him he is worth the whole rotten crowd put together.

phases.label: Former lovers
phases.note: They fell in love in Louisville in 1917.

phases.label: Reunited
phases.note: They meet again over tea at Nick’s house.

phases.label: Affair exposed
phases.note: At the Plaza Gatsby insists Daisy never loved Tom.

phases.label: Rivals for Daisy
phases.note: Tom exposes Gatsby’s bootlegging.

phases.label: Business associates
phases.note: Gatsby admits Wolfsheim fixed the World Series.

phases.label: Patron
phases.note: Gatz served him for five years aboard his yacht.

phases.label: Confidante
phases.note: He takes her aside for a private talk.

phases.label: Intermediary
phases.note: She carries his request that Nick invite Daisy to tea.

phases.label: Killer
phases.note: Believing Gatsby killed Myrtle, Wilson shoots him.

phases.label: Neighbour
phases.note: Chief witness to the accident.

phases.label: Sits with him
phases.note: Stays with Wilson through the night after Myrtle’s death.

phases.label: Fatal accident
phases.note: Driving Gatsby’s car, Daisy strikes and kills Myrtle.
